species.real: Pumping brine out from under Northwich made the ground sink so badly that buildings went up with timber frames that could be jacked back up when the street dropped.
species.name: Brinelet

dex.text: A knobbly lump of rock salt that weeps a little brine when it's nervous. Chips go mad for it. So do slugs, in a much less friendly way.
dex.fact: Cheshire's old salt towns all end in 'wich': Northwich, Middlewich and Nantwich. Salt has been made there from brine springs since Roman times.

species.real: Halite is the mineral name for rock salt, from the Greek hals, salt. The dry caverns at Winsford also store archives and documents, since nothing rots down there.
species.name: Halitor

dex.text: A slab-shouldered pillar of pink and grey salt that lives in the dark under Cheshire and comes up in winter to stand by the roads, looking useful.
dex.fact: The rock salt mine at Winsford in Cheshire has been worked since 1844, and much of the grit spread on Britain's icy roads comes out of it.
